summary: Crow Wing County lookout: 1938 81-ft ladder tower replaced in 1947 by a 90-ft steel tower; listed gone; no removal date or site-today source found.

facts.design: 90-foot steel tower erected 1947 to replace an 81-foot ladder tower
facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it gone; no removal date found in readable sources

staffing.status: Vernon Pratt named in 1947 as in charge of the tower

events.note: First lookout on the site, an 81-foot ladder tower (county catalog)
Old tower dismantled after being declared too old and rickety; new 90-foot steel tower erected near the village of Cuyuna, about half a mile off the Cuyuna-Crosby road
Vernon Pratt named as in charge of the tower (Brainerd Daily Dispatch, August 1947)

map page describes a Cuyuna Lookout Tower in present tense (undated blurb)
evidence.quote: The Cuyuna Lookout Tower stands as a sentinel over the Crow Wing State Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A Pastmaps map blurb describes a Cuyuna Lookout Tower in the present tense, but the blurb is undated and the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone. The association listing is used.
The county catalog says the 1947 tower 'may have been' the first Waskish tower. No other readable source confirms a move, so the story presents it as a guess.

sources.title: Crow Wing County Fire Lookout Towers (Minnesota Forest Service catalog)
Cuyuna - Forest Lookouts (quoting the Brainerd Daily Dispatch, August 28, 1947)

notes_for_editor: The 1947 Brainerd Daily Dispatch report is read second-hand on the Forest Lookouts site; the original paper was not read. The catalog's Waskish link is a guess and is labelled that way in the story. Removal date and site-today are not in any readable source. A Pequot Lakes fire tower article (Southern Minnesota Scene / MPR) surfaced in search but describes a different tower and was not used. The Star Tribune article was rate-limited and not read. Access and visit are omitted because no source gives them.
